findings.title: Gunner Shooting XP is given before the shot starts, so failed casts still give XP
findings.detail: Fire() calls GiveGunnerShootingXp() before base.BeginBurst(). If TryStartCastOn then returns false (no line of sight, out of range, target gone; e.g. a force-target behind a wall), no shot is fired and burstCooldownTicksLeft stays 0. TryStartShootSomething runs again, a new warmup starts, and 170 XP per cycle-second is paid every warmup without a shot. Vanilla gives this XP in Verb_Shoot.WarmupComplete, which only runs after CanHitTarget has passed. Change: in Fire(), replace base.BeginBurst() with `if (AttackVerb.TryStartCastOn(CurrentTarget)) GiveGunnerShootingXp(); OnAttackedTarget(CurrentTarget);`. That is the same two-line body as Building_TurretGun.BeginBurst, with the XP gated on success.

findings.title: Manned mounts lose the weapon's quality damage multiplier and unique-weapon traits
findings.detail: Verb_LaunchProjectile.TryCastShot sets equipmentSource = caster (the mount) whenever CompMannable has a ManningPawn (Verb_LaunchProjectile.cs:93-97). Projectile then reads quality and RangedWeapon_DamageMultiplier from the building, not the weapon (Projectile.cs:196, ProjectileProperties.cs:118), and CompUniqueWeapon traits are looked up on the building too. Automated mounts keep them; manned ones silently fire as a normal-quality gun. The class summary says quality and comps ride along, and BurstCooldownTime does use weapon quality, so the behaviour is inconsistent. Change: correct the class doc comment and the player-facing description so they say this, or accept it knowingly. Restoring it needs a separate patch on the projectile launch, which the corpus does not show anyone doing.

findings.title: A weapon cannot be installed while a gunner is manning the mount
findings.detail: JobDriver_InstallMountedWeapon reserves targetA (the mount), and JobDriver_ManTurret reserves the same building for the gunner (JobDriver_ManTurret.cs:96). The WorkGiver's CanReserve check means there is no error, but a pending weapon is never installed until the gunner leaves, with nothing on screen saying why. Worth an inspect-string hint, or not reserving the mount in TryMakePreToilReservations (the weapon reservation already stops two installers competing).

findings.title: fireReadyTick window can skip the warmup when a forced target is cleared or changed at the very end of a warmup
findings.detail: ResetForcedTarget and OrderAttack (through TryStartShootSomething(false)) set burstWarmupTicksLeft = 1 without clearing fireReadyTick. If that lands within the last couple of ticks of a running warmup, the next BeginBurst falls inside [fireReadyTick, fireReadyTick+2] and fires at once on the new target. The effect is tiny. Clearing fireReadyTick whenever BeginBurst is entered with burstWarmupTicksLeft not having counted down from this mount's own warmup would close it.

findings.title: Destroy(Vanish), or destroying an unspawned (minified) mount, deletes the mounted weapon and core with no refund
findings.detail: The weapon is only taken off when wasSpawned && mode != Vanish. Uninstalling uses DeSpawn, not Destroy, so it is safe. A minified mount destroyed while held as an item, or a Vanish-mode removal, loses a possibly legendary weapon silently. Intentional or not, it is worth knowing.

findings.title: Install work is skipped while the mount cannot be reserved, e.g. if a manned mount's gunner holds it
findings.detail: WorkGiver_InstallMountedWeapon.HasJobOnThing returns false when pawn.CanReserve(mount) fails. If the manning job also reserves the turret (not confirmed: I ran out of tool calls before reading JobDriver_ManTurret), a weapon chosen during combat waits silently until nobody is manning, and a forced order gives no reason. If that is the case, setting JobFailReason.Is(...) before returning false at that check would tell the player why.

findings.title: Mount info cards show the placeholder as their weapon
findings.detail: ThingDef.SpecialDisplayStats lists building.turretGunDef as 'Weapon' with its Weapon_Ranged stats on every turret def. Every mount def's info card will therefore read 'Weapon: empty weapon mount' with range 0. It does no harm, but players may find it confusing. The cheapest fix is to label MW_EmptyMountGun with something like 'installed weapon (choose one)'.

findings.title: IsMortar is decided by the placeholder turretGunDef, so it is always false
findings.detail: BuildingProperties.IsMortar reads turretGunDef's primary verb projectile. MW_EmptyMountGun has none, so a mount never counts as a mortar, and TryFindNewTarget never adds NeedNotUnderThickRoof. Only matters if MountUtility ever accepts a flyOverhead launcher. The roofed-cell refusal in TryStartShootSomething still applies because it checks the live verb.

findings.title: csproj HintPaths are absolute paths under /Users/tirrella
findings.detail: Assembly-CSharp and the UnityEngine references point at this Mac's Steam install, so the project will not build on any other machine or in CI without editing. A relative path or the Krafs.Rimworld.Ref package is the usual portable choice.

findings.title: MW_CoreLost / MW_CoreSurvived put a capitalised label mid-sentence
findings.detail: Both strings read "... the {1}." but the caller passes LabelCap (the `label` local in Destroy, used at the Translate call), so the message reads e.g. "The subcore inside the Automated mount was destroyed with it." Passing `Label` instead of `LabelCap` to {1}, or changing the text so {1} starts the sentence, reads naturally. The text only; nothing breaks.
